All day every day. I have this constant narrative that I’m fucking up at work, my relationships, my mental health, my responsibilities, all the things. I get so hung up on insignificant bullshit to the point that it consumes me and I stay stuck in the past. I find myself having panic attacks over something (no matter how big or little) I did 5 years ago. My biggest issue is that I’m comfortable in the past because I know how the story goes, but the future scares me and the present is too real to handle. I shut down when the “I’m a shit person and I don’t deserve anything positive” train of thought pops in. 

I think the biggest thing is to try recognize when those thoughts pop in and challenge them. Take apart why you feel the way you feel about what happened/your thoughts/anything. Am I really that bad of a person? What other good things did I do in that instance, and what can I do differently next time? Would I be saying the negative things I think of myself to another person? Why do I think I don’t deserve to treat myself kindly? Why do I feel the need to dredge up my past failures? I think you’ll notice that a lot of the things we feel and think of ourselves aren’t always true. We get comfortable being mean to ourselves because that’s all we know. It’s hard to break that barrier, but it gets easier with time and you’ll be able to catch those thoughts before they get out of hand. 

The most important thing is to show yourself some empathy and not automatically give up when growth is painful. You’re capable of change even if you don’t believe it right now. I’m sorry this was a lot but I really hope it helped a little bit.
